A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FPE research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Boolean-DNF and vision-classification experiments, including accuracy, interference measurements, and deeper-network and sparsity experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds joint representation learning, class-count sweeps, DropConnect comparisons, and circuit analyses.

M1.justification: The core disjoint splitting and magnitude re-pruning procedure is retained, including the previously documented deeper-network and structured-sparsity variants. V2 adds model adaptations with a trainable Boolean embedding and a jointly trained CNN feeding the classifier; expansion still operates on the classifier (Section A.7.1).

E1.justification: The Boolean task and four vision dataset families remain. V2 adds raw-image CIFAR-100 classification alongside frozen CLIP features and nested 40/60/80/100-class classification scenarios, expanding input conditions and task coverage within existing domains (Sections 5.2–5.3).

E2.justification: V2 introduces two substantive comparators absent from v1: non-disjoint FPE with a fixed random mask, and DropConnect with resampled training masks and dense scaled test-time weights. Figure A6 and Tables A14–A15 explicitly evaluate these alternatives against FPE.

E3.justification: V1 lists batch size 500 and N=W=1000; v2 specifies batch size 64 with 25 pre-training and 25 fine-tuning epochs, retaining long training for the illustrative example. FashionMNIST warmup changes from 20 to 25 epochs. New experiments introduce matched mask controls and collision/clustering metrics. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds disjointness and mask-resampling controls, edge-collision measurements, clause-recovery analyses, and clustered-Gram case studies (A.8.4–A.9). The expansion-factor sensitivity panel in v1 Figure 6d is replaced by a class-count/width analysis. Depth, dynamic-mask, and 2:4 sparsity analyses were already present and are retained.

E5.justification: The main vision comparisons and Figure 6 now report ten trials where v1 generally reported five; ImageNet-1k already used ten. SEM bars and p<0.05 reporting remain. These reported-count changes do not establish additional runs, and v2's blanket ten-trial statement conflicts with retained five- and 30-trial appendix captions.

E6.justification: V2 revises vision plots and adds substantial joint-learning, class-demand, comparator, and circuit results. For example, Table A14 reports 64.8% for non-disjoint FPE versus 65.8% for FPE at width eight; at width four, the values are 51.0% versus 50.9%. These comparisons are new, while the original illustrative accuracies and several appendix tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The clause-coverage bound and expected collision-reduction derivation in Appendix A.5 are unchanged. V2 adds a distinct edge-level collision-rate definition—the proportion of traced edges used by at least two clauses—in A.9, a limited mathematical definition accompanying the new empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The central fixed-budget interference–performance claim and claimed first explicit demonstration remain. V2 reframes FPE as a controlled mechanistic intervention, explicitly attributes gains to disjoint parameter allocation beyond width alone, and extends its applicability claim to jointly learned representations (Sections 2.2, 5.2, and 7).

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: it discusses disjointness controls, feature demand growing with width, preliminary circuit evidence, small-model scope, and hardware-dependent speedups and activation overhead. Appendix A.5 also explicitly acknowledges that its independent-support analysis does not enforce FPE's disjointness constraint.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-availability link, detailed trainable-embedding and CNN specifications, baseline mask-sampling and inference procedures, and storage-cost discussion. Algorithm A3 explicitly documents pre-training, expansion, and continued training. These additions substantially expand implementation guidance; the linked resource itself was not accessed.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantively distinguishes FPE from sparse autoencoders and DropConnect and discusses compatibility with quantization and distillation. Citations expand accordingly, including Cunningham et al., Wan et al., and GPTQ. This extends research positioning beyond relocating v1's pruning, growth, and superposition discussion.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction and conclusion, adds an explicit contribution list and scope statement, reorganizes methodology, and separates theory, symbolic results, vision results, and related work into distinct sections. The narrative shifts toward using expansion to study interference.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. The framework diagram moves to Appendix A.1, main performance figures are condensed while fuller displays remain in the appendix, and numerous accuracy tables and new control/circuit plots are added. Retained plots are distinguished from newly reported evidence.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked controls isolating disjointness and evidence from jointly learned visual representations. V2 substantially addresses both gaps through Appendix A.8.4 and Section 5.2, while adding more direct circuit diagnostics, implementation guidance, and clearer applicability limits. These additions materially strengthen the central argument. Inconsistent trial-count summaries and preliminary mechanistic evidence remain limitations, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support and transparency.
